Leah (platform): quick heads-up  we're rolling out a 'flag cleanup' capability next week to remove long-deprecated runtime flags. Goal: reduce config noise and avoid stale gating. Planning a preview -> canary -> full run sequence. Can we align on safety controls?
Diego (runtime): sounds good. Needs to be conservative. What qualifies as removable?
Leah (platform): proposal: flags with `deprecated:true` AND `last_used_ts < now-90d` AND not marked `safety:critical`. Skip flags where `owner` is null.
Anika (infra): please exclude infra-level toggles (lb, rollout keys, network shims) by default. Also want a bulk-owner lookup so we don't hammer the ownership service.
Ravi (ops): ops requirements: 1) dry-run preview that produces per-service diffs; 2) canary application to a shadow config store for 1 hour with real traffic; 3) cohorted rollout 10%/50%/100% with metric gates.
Leah (platform): API sketch for internal use:
```
POST /v1/internal/configs/cleanup
{ "dry_run": true, "services": ["payments","ingest"], "cohort_pct": 10, "owners_override": false }
GET /v1/internal/configs/cleanup/{id}/preview
```
Diego (runtime): runtime will provide `is_cleanup_candidate(flag)` predicate that checks owner, safety, last_used_ts. We'll also wire a bulk endpoint `/v1/flags/bulk-owners?names=...` per Anika.
Anika (infra): bulk endpoint will return `{name, owners, regions}` and rate-limit headers. We'll also tag region-scoped flags; skip them unless owner approves.
Ravi (ops): metric gates: primary = error_rate delta (1m & 5m windows), p95 latency delta, and 5xx rate. Thresholds: error_rate +1% OR p95 +50ms OR 5xx +0.5% -> auto-pause and roll back cohort. Also require manual approval if a service has >5 deletions.
Leah (platform): good. Console will show preview diffs with owner badges, per-flag metadata, and 'bulk approve' per service. Add an emergency pause button that sets `config.cleanup.pause=true`. Also include a permalink to the dry-run JSON for audit.
Diego (runtime): implementation note: we should snapshot pre-change state to `cleanup_snapshot_{id}.json` and keep for 30 days. Also support `POST /v1/internal/configs/cleanup/{id}/rollback` that restores snapshot into the runtime store.
Anika (infra): ownership-missing flow: route a notification to `#ownerless-flags` with a short link to the preview. Default behavior: skip ownerless flags. If `owners_override=true` then require two approvers in the console (explicit approver IDs).
Ravi (ops): shadow-store idea: create a shadow config namespace and apply removals there, then run a 1-hour canary traffic pass. If no regressions, proceed to cohort percentages. This keeps rollback cheap.
Leah (platform): MVP will be preview + snapshot + cohorted commits + console approvals + telemetry. Shadow-store can be opt-in for the first few customers.
Diego (runtime): telemetry events: `cleanup.preview`, `cleanup.apply.cohort`, `cleanup.finalize`, include counts, service, sweep_id, operator_id. Emit pre/post metrics snapshot so infra can evaluate regressions.
Anika (infra): add region-awareness: if a flag is only seen in eu-west-1, skip unless owner approves. Also ensure the bulk-owner endpoint can annotate `region_scope`.
Ravi (ops): rollback cadence: immediate rollback for cohort failures, and a 'grace period' where snapshot is retained for 30d. After that we can permanently delete artifacts.
Leah (platform): security: keep all cleanup endpoints internal-only and RBAC gated (platform-admins + ops-runbooks). We'll expose `redwoodctl cleanup preview --id sw-...` for CLI users.
